question.text: For listed REIT units sold on a recognised stock exchange with STT paid, where the holding period is 12 months or less, the Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG) rate applicable under Section 111A is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Level 2 workbook (pages 280, 283), STCG on listed REIT/InvIT units transferred on a recognised stock exchange with STT paid is taxed under Section 111A. The applicable STCG rate is 20% (post the rate revision applicable to Section 111A short-term gains on equity-like instruments). The Trap: 15% is the older Section 111A rate that candidates may carry over from earlier study material. 'Slab rate' applies to transactions outside Section 111A (for example, off-market sales without STT). 'Exempt due to grandfathering' is incorrect - grandfathering affects the cost computation for long-term gains under Section 112A; it is not an exemption from tax. Note: Listed REIT / InvIT units held for more than 12 months and sold with STT fall under Section 112A as LTCG, not Section 111A. The current Section 111A rate of 20% is the source-supported answer for the STCG question itself.
